content.comment_body: What is the voltage limit for inputs and outputs on [product_name] [version_no]? I need to be sure about these specifications. The technical data folder mentions power supply range and maximum current for relay contacts (both inductive and resistive loads). For digital inputs, it appears the supply voltage limit applies. For digital outputs, I am unsure if I can use voltages like 220, 380, 440, or 760 VAC. Is this related to the isolation voltage limit? Thanks!
Manuals for [product_name] can be found here: [url]. Depending on your [product_name], there are different limits for inputs and outputs.

From my experience (others may have more detailed knowledge), I recommend using [product_name] with 24VDC inputs and outputs, and separate relays that match the voltage you need to switch. I would not use a controller to directly switch 760VAC, for example; the maximum I would allow is 120/230VAC for direct switching.

Hi, A [product_name] 24 has this range for power supply and inputs: 20.4V DC to 28.8V DC. Transistor outputs: Voltage: equal to or less than power supply. Current: max 0.3A. The relay outputs on [product_name] are all the same; here is an extract from the manual. Hope this helps.
[user_name], very clear information, thank you. The irony is, I already had this manual.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are looking for clear guidance on voltage limits for digital inputs and outputs with [product_name] [version_no]. There is confusion about whether high AC voltages (e.g., 220V or 760V) can be switched directly, or if external relays are needed. While documentation is referenced, users find it difficult to interpret, revealing a lack of accessible and straightforward voltage specification information in the product materials.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect simple and direct information about the safe voltage limits for both inputs and outputs, with specific attention to whether high AC voltages can be used directly with [product_name] [version_no].
